description: Make agent.run({ skipPermissions: true }) a truthful, child-scoped permission-bypass contract across standalone and Factory Session execution, provider capability checks, public JavaScript contracts, and durable recordings so capable routes honor bypass and incapable routes fail before execution.

context.customerAsk: Deliver all four stories from the JavaScript Child Permission Override Plan as one prerequisite lane: propagate skipPermissions through the standalone provider boundary, define precedence over policy.mode, add truthful Claude/Codex/Agy/ACP bypass capability behavior with pre-execution failure for incapable routes, and publish the field in JavaScript contracts, reference documentation, dispatch observations, recordings, and replay. Accommodate the post-PR #1862 execution test layout and follow the mandatory rebase protocol.
context.problem: The standalone direct child executor records skipPermissions but drops it before ProviderInferenceRequest, so unattended child work can stall on approvals the author explicitly waived. Policy precedence is implicit, unsupported providers can silently ignore bypass, and published and recorded surfaces do not fully describe or retain the requested behavior.
context.solution: Preserve the optional boolean through normalization, policy resolution, both child execution compositions, provider selection, and durable observation. Treat true as a per-child override of provider approval and sandbox restrictions while retaining unrelated policy limits. Let Providers truthfully declare and apply bypass support, reject unsupported routes before any execution side effect, and align authored contracts, generated projections, documentation, events, recordings, resume, and replay.

acceptanceCriteria: Static and dynamically constructed agent.run requests preserve boolean skipPermissions values through standalone and canonical Factory Session execution; omission and false reach providers as false.

Under every recognized policy.mode, skipPermissions: true overrides only provider approval and sandbox restrictions for the addressed child; unrelated policy controls remain enforced and siblings retain their own effective policy.

Claude, Codex, Agy, and ACP routes truthfully apply their supported bypass behavior, while any selected route that cannot honor bypass fails with a stable, safe capability diagnostic before an attempt or provider side effect starts.

Authored JavaScript contracts, generated projections, reference documentation, dispatch events, recordings, resume, and replay consistently expose and preserve the child-scoped boolean without leaking prompts, credentials, or raw command lines.

Focused and functional regression evidence proves a capable route receives bypass, an incapable route fails closed pre-execution, and the standalone executor carries true into ProviderInferenceRequest; the standalone case includes red-on-main evidence in the PR.

Typecheck, focused and required tests pass; there are no NEW lint violations relative to current main, and the gates green on main (backend-size, pkg-maint, pkg-file-count, pkg-structure, vet) stay green.
The implementation/review loop continues until required CI is terminal and passing, all blocking PR conversation feedback is explicitly addressed, merge conflicts are resolved, and the PR is merged.

userStories.title: Preserve bypass at every provider boundary
userStories.description: As a JavaScript workflow author, I want the child permission-bypass value to reach the provider identically from standalone and Factory Session execution so unattended behavior does not depend on composition.
acceptanceCriteria: Static and dynamically constructed agent.run objects preserve skipPermissions: true through normalization and dispatch.
The supported standalone JavaScript composition passes true into the resulting ProviderInferenceRequest; a focused provider-boundary regression test fails on current main and passes with the change.
The canonical Factory Runtime, Worker Sessions, Workers, and Providers path remains equivalent at the provider boundary.
Omission and explicit false arrive at the provider boundary as false in both compositions.
Tests follow the post-PR #1862 execution test layout and assert observable provider requests rather than intermediate struct topology.
Typecheck passes
Tests pass
userStories.notes: Preserved skipPermissions in the standalone directChildExecutor ProviderInferenceRequest mapping. Expanded observable regression coverage for static and dynamic agent.run objects, standalone true/false/omitted requests, and canonical Factory Runtime -> Worker Sessions -> Workers true/false/omitted requests. Red-on-baseline evidence: removing the standalone mapping made TestDirectChildExecutor_CarriesSkipPermissionsToProviderInferenceRequest/true observe false. Focused boundary, normalization, validation, and diff checks pass; typecheck and affected package suites are recorded in progress.txt.

userStories.title: Define child-scoped precedence over policy mode
userStories.description: As a workflow author, I want an explicit per-child bypass to override approval and sandbox restrictions without weakening other workflow policy or sibling behavior.
acceptanceCriteria: Every recognized policy.mode accepts a boolean skipPermissions: true on a child request and does not deny that child solely for provider approval or sandbox restrictions.
Model and reasoning allowlists plus fanout, concurrency, duration, token, and other resource budgets continue to reject requests that exceed policy.
A sibling that omits the field continues through normal policy evaluation, and one child's override never mutates session-global state.
Resume and replay restore the authored value on the corresponding child dispatch without applying it to siblings or later children.
The precedence rule and retained policy limits are documented in the owning runtime contract and covered across all recognized modes.
Typecheck passes
Tests pass
userStories.notes: Carried skipPermissions into the shared child-policy request and defined it as a child-scoped override. The READ_ONLY mode (the only currently recognized JavaScript policy mode) now permits the addressed child’s sandbox and writable-root restrictions when skipPermissions is true, while model, reasoning, command, network, concurrency, fanout, session, duration, token, output, and artifact controls remain policy-owned; siblings retain independent evaluation. Resume/replay coverage restores true and false per dispatch. Focused policy and runtime suites pass, and the owning JavaScript runtime documentation states the precedence and retained controls.

userStories.title: Fail closed using provider capability truth
userStories.description: As an operator, I want the selected provider route either to honor the requested bypass or reject it before execution so the system never silently degrades an autonomous child request.
acceptanceCriteria: Provider-owned capability resolution represents whether the selected route can honor permission bypass and is evaluated before an attempt, subprocess, ACP prompt, or other provider side effect starts.
Claude emits --dangerously-skip-permissions, Codex emits --dangerously-bypass-approvals-and-sandbox, and Agy emits its supported dangerous permission-bypass option when requested.
ACP selects the existing allow/bypass permission behavior when requested and declares that behavior through the same truthful capability decision.

A route without bypass support returns a stable capability-mismatch outcome before child execution; the diagnostic identifies the provider and missing bypass capability without prompt, credential, or raw-command disclosure.
A functional test proves skipPermissions: true reaches a capable route with bypass enabled and that an incapable route fails before its execution edge is invoked.
Omission and false preserve existing provider defaults and do not require bypass capability.
Typecheck passes
Tests pass
userStories.notes: Added provider-owned permission_bypass capability projection from authored Claude/Codex/Agy manifests and ACP integration descriptors. Providers validates requested bypass before live-attempt binding, readiness probes, subprocess launch, external integration invocation, or ACP prompt handling; unsupported routes return a stable capability-mismatch failure naming only the provider and missing capability. Claude, Codex, and Agy retain their dangerous bypass flags, ACP retains allow/bypass behavior, external registrations carry the request, and worker/MCP failure mappings stay safe. Added root-boundary functional coverage for the capable Codex command route and a real registered-but-incapable Codex route modeled through an Edges catalog capability override, with zero command-edge calls; provider-root and neutral-registry mismatch regressions remain in place. Request-time negotiated capabilities are now checked immediately before every external or conductor Invoke, with omitted permission_bypass mapped to the same stable safe mismatch and zero invocation regression coverage. Generated OpenAPI/package projections are synchronized; typecheck, affected suites, structure/maintainability gates, vet, drift, and catalog checks pass.

userStories.title: Publish and record the bypass contract
userStories.description: As an author or operator, I want to discover and inspect the child-scoped bypass request so I can author workflows correctly and explain execution from durable history.
acceptanceCriteria: Static and dynamic validation accept only a boolean skipPermissions; a non-boolean value fails before dispatch with the existing safe field-level diagnostic shape.

The authored JavaScript symbol catalog, agent.run call-behavior descriptor, schema, examples, typed error behavior, contracts/javascript/runtime-api.json, and generated package projection include the optional field.

Reference documentation describes the field as a dangerous child-level override, its precedence over provider approval and sandbox restrictions, its provider-capability requirement, and the routing and resource controls it does not disable.
Dispatch events, records, recordings, resume, and replay retain the requested boolean for the corresponding child without exposing raw provider command lines or sensitive payloads.
Preview may warn when literal true is detected but does not reject it because of policy.mode.
Contract generation and checks plus documentation smoke tests verify customer-visible behavior and generated projections remain aligned.
Typecheck passes
Tests pass
userStories.notes: Published the optional boolean in the authored JavaScript runtime catalog/schema, installed call-behavior descriptor and baseline, generated package projection, OpenAPI dispatch/event projections, and reference docs. Added the typed non-boolean diagnostic and observable preview/runtime coverage. JavaScript child dispatch records now feed the public Dispatch projection and canonical DISPATCH_QUEUED event with explicit true/false retention; recordings, world-state projection, resume snapshots, and ReplayDispatchProjection preserve the corresponding child value without prompts or raw commands. Added canonical recording/replay and Factory Session projection assertions. Corrected the public contract wording so incapable routes are documented as failing after child dispatch is recorded but before provider execution side effects, then regenerated the package artifact and content-addressed manifest digest. Contract validation/checks, docs smoke, interface generation, typecheck, focused suites, verify-fast, maintainability/file-count/structure gates, and go vet all pass.
